scope: Original Nemesis, English 28-page manual basic board, standard semi-cooperative game with six original Characters; official FAQ v2.2 printed pp.2-4 base-game Rules/Actions/Rooms/Items, excluding Rules17-18 and Actions16. PL/FR/DE original manuals are compatible supplements, not automatically subordinate. Optional modes, alternative boards, expansions and campaign excluded.

method.pdf_inspection: Checked page-extracted PDF text against English and FAQ extractions; inspected readable embedded illustrations for dice faces, Item/Action-card examples, Craft icons, and Room tiles. PL/FR/DE PDFs and corresponding reading texts were hash-verified and used as compatible supplemental evidence at material branches, including Egg Melee miss wording and Pod procedure.
method.author_map_role: Challengeable coverage map only; findings were checked against permitted primary passages.
method.accepted_Q19_scope: The clean accepted scope file was applied as fixed; no re-adjudication.

question_audit.actual_request: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?
How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?

You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?
A Character in a burning Room takes one Action then passes. When do they take Fire damage, can they act again this Player Phase, can they discard cards, and do later players rounds burn them again?
Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
What does Careful Movement cost and replace, when is it forbidden, and can a Closed Door be crossed or a miniature stop in a Corridor?

You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?
How does Danger resolve with several eligible neighboring Intruders, and when none are eligible? Does moving an Intruder into your Room count as an Encounter? How does Slime affect Silence?
During an Encounter you draw Blank. What happens to Noise and the Blank; when is an Adult added? Contrast Blank in bag development.

Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.
After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?
A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?

At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?
question_audit.note: The ordinary successful Melee draw and the Egg miss waiver are supported; exact ordering/refund mechanics are not specified and the key correctly avoids inventing them.

question_audit.actual_request: After successfully boarding an Escape Pod, may you launch immediately rather than wait? When it launches now or on a later turn, what happens to the Pod token and occupants’ miniatures, and do those occupants continue taking part in active play?
question_audit.topic: Escape Pod launch procedure and removal from active play
question_audit.note: Distinct launch resolution is supported by English printed page 26; one key PDF reference incorrectly says page 25.

findings.actual_stem: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
keyed_closest_clauses: Enter then launch immediately or wait and pass current turn.
At start of first round next Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or free exit followed by a full two-Action round.
Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants; another boarder may immediately launch.
missing_requested_parts: A waiting Character remains treated as present in the Evacuation Section and performs the Adult bag-development Noise roll.
A Malfunction placed while a Character is already waiting does not remove that Character’s launch, wait, or exit choices; it only blocks new entry.

primary_evidence.passage: The Character is treated like present in the Room, so they perform Noise roll in such case.

Nothing. The Character inside an Escape pod may still launch the Escape pod, wait, or exit the Escape pod. The Malfunction marker only disallows use of the Evacuation Section Room (entering the Escape Pods).

findings.distinct_consequence: The first omission changes exposure to an Encounter while waiting; the second changes whether an already-boarded passenger can leave or launch after a Malfunction. Both are required by the fixed Q19 literal scope, even though Q63 and Q64 separately retain bank-level coverage.

findings.issue: Each answer cites source-snapshot.txt, which is not among the ten permitted primary source files; the cited extraction line ranges correspond to the supplied extracted/nemesis-rules.txt and the factual answers are independently supported there. This is provenance metadata, not a factual-answer defect.
The key cites nemesis-original-rules.pdf printed page 25 for the Escape Pods launch passage; that passage is on printed/PDF page 26. Its extracted/nemesis-rules.txt reference 2705-2718 is correct.

closest_actual_requests_and_keyed_clause.stem: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?

closest_actual_requests_and_keyed_clause.stem: For a rule concerned with the Character's arrival on Earth, where is a Character in a launched Escape Pod treated as having arrived? Does this establish that the ship itself reached Earth?
closest_actual_requests_and_keyed_clause.key_clause: Any Character in a launched Escape Pod is always treated as having arrived on Earth.

closest_actual_requests_and_keyed_clause.stem: What ends the game when Time runs out or the last active Character leaves/dies/hibernates; how is an active Self-Destruct resolved and do Intruders die from a normal jump?
closest_actual_requests_and_keyed_clause.key_clause: Last alive non-hibernating aboard leaves/dies/hibernates: advance active Self-Destruct to final red and destroy ship, else advance Time final red and jump.

primary_evidence.passage: If you launch immediately (or if you launch in one of the following turns) – remove the miniature of your Character and the Escape Pod token from the game. From now on, you do not take part in the game any longer.

candidate_ledger.distinct_consequence: Q128 expressly asks the physical removal of the Pod and occupants and the end of active participation after immediate or later launch. These are not required by Q19’s fixed waiting scope, Q62’s Earth-status question, or Q49’s endgame trigger.

candidate_ledger.candidate: One more waiting Pod contingency or second occupant quantity
candidate_ledger.reason: Q19 fixed scope covers first and later waiting choices, second-boarder launch, Intruder return, and Malfunction permissions; Q63 directly covers bag-development Noise; Q64 directly covers Malfunction; Q128 covers launch removal. Another occupant/time instance adds no distinct consequence.

candidate_ledger.candidate: Danger with every Corridor already noisy

primary_evidence.passage: If there are no Corridors you can put Noise markers in, nothing happens.

candidate_ledger.reason: Q08 asks what happens with no eligible neighboring Intruders and keys placement only in connected Corridors lacking Noise; with none lacking, the requested operation has no placement. Q111 resolves Technical Corridor shared-marker scope.

candidate_ledger.candidate: General Hand Serious Wound effect on Item Actions

primary_evidence.passage: No, because Shoot is a Basic action, not an Item action.

candidate_ledger.reason: The FAQ establishes exclusions for Basic Shoot and Scout Motion Scanner, already directly asked. The complete Serious Wound card text is not in the readable supplied corpus; this premise alone does not justify a new scored full positive-effect procedure or exact cost.

primary_evidence.passage: Dress 1 Serious Wound OR Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound.

candidate_ledger.reason: Dress versus Heal, treatment of Dressed Serious Wounds, OR selection, and permission to use Medkit on others are already requested. The illustrated card adds a carrier and subset, without a further exception or outcome.

candidate_ledger.candidate: One more Egg Melee miss execution order or Nest replenishment after destruction

primary_evidence.passage: In the case of a Melee Attack Action, the Character does not draw a Contamination card or suffer Wounds if they miss.

candidate_ledger.reason: The ordinary pre-roll Melee draw and miss-only waiver leave the exact miss execution timing unspecified. No supplied rule gives a destroyed-Nest replenishment procedure. Q18 correctly preserves this limit; do not invent an outcome.

candidate_ledger.candidate: All eight Adult models already in Combat fallback

primary_evidence.passage: Remove all Adult Intruder models that are not in Combat and put the corresponding Intruder tokens back in the Intruder bag (if possible). Then, place an Adult Intruder model in the Room where Encounter occured.

candidate_ledger.reason: The text supplies no executable way to free a model when all eight are in Combat; Q51 explicitly marks that limit.

candidate_ledger.candidate: Further illustrated card names, costs, and quantities
candidate_ledger.reason: Readable examples support existing requested mechanics. Another carrier or numeric variant alone is insufficient; tiny examples and the missing complete physical-card corpus do not support a complete-card-effect claim.

closure_verdict.retained_coverage: No further distinct, material, source-backed requested procedure/outcome/exception/information boundary established beyond the exact 126-question bank under the stated primary-source and scope limits.
closure_verdict.key_readiness: Q19 expected_answer needs two missing waiting consequences from the fixed accepted scope; Q58-Q62 and Q128 citation metadata need repair. No other material factual key error was established.
closure_verdict.boundedness: This is bounded coverage closure for the readable supplied original core manual and 61 scoped current-FAQ entries, not a claim of complete physical-card corpus, every hypothetical state, or unsupported source-gap resolution.

unchanged_global_source_core_limits: The author ledger records four essential source gaps. This review does not close or invent rulings for them; the candidate ledger identifies concrete unresolved examples established from the supplied passages.
Some illustrated card clauses are too small or incomplete to read confidently; the supplied examples are not a complete physical-card corpus.
Alternative board, solo/cooperative/intruder modes, campaign and expansions remain excluded.
PL/FR/DE manuals were treated as compatible supplemental wording; no automatic English precedence or language-only erratum was presumed.
